claim_statement: GRABMyo raw cohort contains 43 participants across 3 sessions with 30,715 verified files.
Full-channel LOSO Macro-F1 is 0.542 for XGBoost and 0.538 for SVM across 43 participants.
XGBoost and RBF-SVM are statistically indistinguishable at full channel baseline (p=0.154).
Random Forest is significantly inferior to both XGBoost and SVM (p<0.001).
SVM reported performance is a lower bound limited by 40k window subsampling.
Pre-registered primary non-inferiority margin is delta = 0.02 Macro-F1.
Minimal non-inferior channel count is k* = 12 channels (LCB95 = -0.0152 > -0.020).
Sensor reduction below k=12 fails non-inferiority (k=11 LCB = -0.0208 <= -0.020).
Between-subject attribution stability across individual participants shows mean Spearman rho = 0.927.
Primary flexor (Ch 1, 9) and extensor (Ch 5, 13) channels have selection frequency > 95%.
Multi-day donning/doffing causes a performance drop of 0.067 to 0.076 Macro-F1.
Multi-day exposure in training (CS2) recovers performance on Session 3 to 0.486.
ROAR deletion curves confirm functional ordering (F1_top < F1_random < F1_bottom).
NinaPro DB5 external replication confirms methodological validity on 10 subjects and 12 movements.
Bipolar sensitivity analysis (8 channels) confirms consistency under differential derivation.
